SUPERSONIC.Definition: faster than the speed of sound

MERE.Definition: only (showing how small an amount is)

EVENTUAL.Definition: happening at the end of a long process; final

DOWNFALL.Definition: a sudden loss of success or power; ruin

ACCESSIBLE.Definition: available; possible to get or use

LEGACY CARRIERS.Definition: the old, established airlines that existed before cheap airlines

PRIVILEGED.Definition: having special advantages because of wealth or position

IN-FLIGHT.Definition: served while the plane is in the air

FREE-FLOWING.Definition: available in large amounts, without any limit

ALTITUDE.Definition: height above the ground or sea

TURBULENCE.Definition: sudden, rough movements of the air that shake a plane

VASTLY.Definition: very greatly; by a huge amount

DEREGULATION.Definition: the removal of government rules and controls

FEAT.Definition: an achievement that needs great skill or effort

EMPHASISED.Definition: drew attention to; made more noticeable

EXCEPTIONAL.Definition: much greater or better than normal

BACK UP.Definition: go back a little to an earlier point in the story

BLUEPRINT.Definition: a detailed plan or drawing for building something

LAUNCH.Definition: the first time something new is put into use

SNAG.Definition: a problem or difficulty, often an unexpected one

BANKRUPT.Definition: unable to pay its debts; without money

RATION BOOKS.Definition: official papers that limited how much food each person could buy

REMARKABLY.Definition: surprisingly; in a way that people notice

COLLABORATION.Definition: working together with others on a shared project

RIVAL.Definition: be as good as, or compete with

PROTOTYPE.Definition: a first model of something, made to test the design

MAIDEN.Definition: very first (used about a journey by a plane or ship)

VOYAGE.Definition: a long journey; here, a flight

BOMBER.Definition: a military plane built to drop explosives on targets

NON-SUPERSONIC.Definition: not able to fly faster than the speed of sound

BEAK.Definition: the hard, pointed mouth of a bird

TILTING.Definition: leaning or sloping at an angle

LINE OF SIGHT.Definition: view; what someone can see in front of them

WING.Definition: one of the long flat parts on each side of a plane that help it fly

DRAG.Definition: the force of air pushing against a moving object and slowing it down

ABSURD.Definition: so great that it seems almost silly

SUSTAIN.Definition: keep at the same level for a long time

CURVE.Definition: a gently bending, rounded line or shape

PRIVILEGE.Definition: a special chance or advantage that only a few people have

MIRACULOUS.Definition: so amazing that it seems almost impossible

DELICACIES.Definition: rare or expensive foods that are special to eat

LOBSTER.Definition: a large sea creature with a hard shell and claws, eaten as luxury food

CAVIAR.Definition: the salted eggs of a large fish, eaten as an expensive food

DRUM UP.Definition: collect or find, with some effort

BURST.Definition: a sudden, short period of something; also (verb): broke open suddenly

CRUISING ALTITUDE.Definition: the steady height at which a plane flies for most of a journey

OYSTER.Definition: a sea creature with a rough flat shell, often eaten raw as luxury food

INTRIGUE.Definition: a sense of mystery and excitement that makes people interested

GLAMOUR.Definition: an attractive, exciting quality linked with wealth and fame

CONVENIENCE.Definition: the quality of being quick and easy, and saving time

SONIC BOOM.Definition: a sudden, very loud noise made when an aircraft travels faster than sound

ADDING INSULT TO INJURY.Definition: making a bad situation even worse, in an unfair way

DISRUPTIVE.Definition: causing problems and stopping normal activity

BOOM.Definition: a deep, very loud noise like an explosion

EXHAUST.Definition: the waste gases that come out of an engine

OZONE LAYER.Definition: a band of gas high in the sky that protects the earth from harmful sunlight

CRANK UP.Definition: raise sharply; increase by a lot

CHARTER.Definition: hire for their own private use

DEVASTATING.Definition: terrible, causing great shock and sadness

CHAIN.Definition: a series of connected events, each causing the next

STRUCTURAL.Definition: relating to how much the body of the plane could safely carry

OVERFUELED.Definition: filled with too much of the liquid that powers the engines

HOLD.Definition: the space in a plane where bags are stored

FREAK ACCIDENT.Definition: a very rare and unlucky event that nobody could expect

TAXIING.Definition: moving along the ground on its wheels

TYRES.Definition: the thick, round rubber coverings on wheels

RUBBER.Definition: a strong material that stretches and bends, used for making tyres

DOOMED.Definition: certain to die or be destroyed

RELAUNCH.Definition: return to service after a pause

APPEAL.Definition: the quality that makes something attractive or interesting

DIPPED.Definition: fell or dropped for a time

CABIN.Definition: the area inside a plane where passengers sit

BUY UP.Definition: purchase as many as possible of

SUCCESSOR.Definition: something that comes next and takes its place

SUBSONIC.Definition: slower than the speed of sound

CAPABILITIES.Definition: skills and powers; what someone is able to do
